sources.citation: Reynolds, Troy. 2025. Ngadju Verbs: A Fresh Approach. Paper presented at Language Sovereignty conference, Karlkurla WA, 21-23 Oct 2025. GALCAC. 20 pp.
sources.note: Only stress remark (p.6, sec. 4.1): reports that von Brandenstein (1980) claims a continuative verb form '*nyinananu.. instead become e.g. nyinakan with stress on the last syllable, however no further argument or evidence is provided' -- a second-hand morphophonological detail, not a word-stress rule.

sources.citation: Goldfields Aboriginal Language Centre Aboriginal Corporation. 2023. Mirniny Phonology (web page, wangka.com.au/mirniny-phonology/), section 7 'Stress'. Not in the READALL 'works' list; already saved by the earlier reading.
sources.note: Describes Mirniny (mirn1238), a different language of the same subgroup (Thieberger 1993 entry 4.1.3: O'Grady et al. 1966 treat Karlaku and Mirning as West and East Mirning; Tindale links a western Mirning dialect with Ngatjumaya). Not evidence for Ngadjunmaya; recorded here only as the nearest open statement.
